metric.why: PPAs are how the boom finances new generation and how operators back renewable claims. Nuclear agreements, including restarts and small modular commitments, became the signature deals of the AI era.
metric.definition: Long-term contracts by which operators secure generation, nuclear, solar, wind, or gas, for current and future facilities.

reading.body:
Power purchase agreements are how AI operators guarantee the electricity their facilities need, and they reveal whether that growth will strain grids or add generation capacity.

Data center operators now sign long-term contracts for nuclear, solar, wind, and gas generation to secure power for current and future facilities. These agreements matter because they show whether the industry is simply bidding up scarce existing power or funding new generation to match its demand. Nuclear deals, including reactor restarts and small modular reactor commitments, have become the dominant signature of this era.

The data captures intentions and commitments but not outcomes. A PPA shows what operators say they will build or buy, not whether new generation will actually reach the grid in time, whether it will cost what the contract assumed, or whether regulatory approval will materialize. The binding constraint on AI scaling depends on whether these agreements translate into energized capacity faster than queued load grows.

siblings.label: Approval to energize versus queued load
